newsitem.title: USA: Daughter of late author Dorris sues, alleging abuse.
newsitem.headline: Daughter of late author Dorris sues, alleging abuse.

text.p: The 21-year-old adopted daughter of author Michael Dorris, who committed suicide last month, has sued his estate alleging he subjected her to years of abuse, the woman's lawyer said on Friday.

The suit filed on Thursday in Minnesota's Hennepin County Court on behalf of Madeleine Dorris demanded at least $50,000 in damages and also names Dorris's former wife and collaborator Louise Erdrich as a defendant, attorney Jeffrey Anderson said.

"The public persona of Michael Dorris was a paradigm of parental virtue, but the private person is the opposite. He abused emotionally and sexually (his adopted children) Abel, Jeffrey, Madeleine, and I believe his two older biological children as well," Anderson said.

The suit alleged that Madeleine, who lives in poverty in Denver on psychiatric disability payments, was sexually, physically and emotionally abused by Dorris between 1980 and 1987, and that Erdrich witnessed the abuse.

The abuse allegedly continued until Madeleine reached age 12, when she was sent to various boarding schools and became estranged from and lived in fear of Dorris. The author's will, which enters probate next week, was revised near the time of his suicide to leave out Madeleine and Erdrich, he said.
Erdrich denied any role in the alleged abuse in an interview with the St. Paul Pioneer Press.

Dorris committed suicide in New Hampshire on April 14, effectively ending a police investigation that he abused his biological children. Erdrich has asked authorities to seal the investigation records.

Dorris gained fame and riches with his book "The Broken Cord," which brought attention to the problem of foetal alcohol syndrome, after adopting three Native American children, including Madeleine, a Sioux. He married Erdrich, with whom he had three daughters, in 1981. His son Abel was hit by a car and killed six years ago.
